storyboard.ears: Where a child learns can decide whether a teacher has time.
India has 127.5 million secondary pupils. Managing that scale can stretch any school system.
storyboard.eyes: substance: pupils with backpacks; cause: Data drags the school's iron gate open by hand and the crowd waiting outside walks into the yard
storyboard.evidence: World Bank | General pupils secondary education | https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SE.SEC.ENRL.GC | 2026-11-21

storyboard.ears: Guinea-Bissau has 147.6 tertiary students per teacher. Individual attention becomes scarce.
storyboard.eyes: substance: students filling the seats; cause: Data carries a desk row up the aisle and sets it down, and each row he places fills with students

storyboard.ears: Education spending fell to 3.57 percent of national income. Expanding schools have less room to improve.
storyboard.evidence: World Bank | Total government expenditure on education | https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SE.XPD.TOTL.GD.ZS | 2026-11-21

storyboard.ears: Youth female literacy reached 92 percent. Expanded schooling can still produce life-changing gains.
storyboard.evidence: World Bank | Youth female literacy rate | https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SE.ADT.1524.LT.FE.ZS | 2026-11-21

storyboard.ears: Tanzania has 114 preschool pupils per teacher. The attention gap starts before primary school.
School scale shapes how much time and support each child can receive.
